title: Layer weakness-specific work on top of fundamentals
summary: A solid routine usually keeps a broad fundamentals base while adding a smaller block aimed at the current weak family or subskill.
why: A fundamentals base keeps general mouse control moving forward.
A smaller weakness-specific overlay lets the player attack the current bottleneck without making the routine too narrow.
actions: Keep a stable fundamentals block, then add one weakness-specific block that targets the current lowest family or subskill.
Use the overlay for a week or more before deciding whether it is helping.
If the routine feels chaotic, remove extra side goals until one weakness overlay remains.
avoid: Do not rebuild the whole routine every session around whatever felt bad that day.

drills.label: Contrast family block
drills.reason: A contrast block widens transfer while still keeping the current weakness in focus.

evidence.claim: Fundamentals plus weakness-specific routines are more effective than replacing broad training with whatever benchmark felt worst that day.
evidence.excerpt: The Voltaic getting-started guide separates fundamentals from weakness-specific work.
